findings.title: canManage() for groups treats VIEW permission as MANAGE permission
findings.body: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() (no-arg), when the admin role check fails, the code calls `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)` instead of checking only the MANAGE scope. This means any admin who was granted only a VIEW permission on the 'all-groups' (or an individual group that falls back to the all-groups resource) will pass `canManage()`. This method gates mutating operations such as `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup()` (`auth.groups().requireManage()`), so a user with read-only access to groups can create/manage groups - a privilege escalation. Compare with `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(GroupModel group)` which correctly checks only `AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE`, and with `UserPermissionEvaluator#canManage()`'s javadoc which only mentions MANAGE. The added javadoc on `GroupPermissionEvaluator#canManage()` documents this VIEW/MANAGE behavior as intentional, which is misleading and should be corrected along with the implementation.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() uses Resource's internal id instead of the group id
findings.body: In `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`, the iteration does `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, groupResource -> { if (hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)) { granted.add(groupResource.getId()); } })`. However, per `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource`/`resolveGroup`, the actual group id is stored as the resource's *name*, not its (randomly generated) *id*. `hasPermission(groupId, ...)` subsequently does `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`, so passing `groupResource.getId()` will never find the per-group resource and will always fall back to the 'all-groups' schema resource evaluation. Consequently: (1) per-group permissions are effectively ignored for this method, with results only reflecting whether an 'all-groups' permission exists for any of the requested scopes, and (2) the returned Set contains internal resource IDs rather than real group IDs. These IDs are used verbatim by callers such as `UsersResource.getUsersCount(realm, search, groupIds)` and session attribute `UserModel.GROUPS`, so downstream filtering by group membership is broken (counts/filters will not match real groups). It should use `groupResource.getName()` both for the permission check and for the value added to the result set.

findings.title: Removed global-view short-circuit causes a per-group authorization evaluation
findings.body: Previously `canViewGlobal = groupsEvaluator.canView()` was computed once and used as `g -> canViewGlobal || groupsEvaluator.canView(g)`, so when the caller has a blanket view permission, no further per-group evaluation was needed. The change to `stream.filter(groupsEvaluator::canView)` removes this optimization: for FGAP V2 (`GroupPermissionsV2.canView(GroupModel)`), each call performs a fresh policy-engine evaluation (`hasPermission(group.getId(), VIEW, MANAGE)`) per group instead of reusing a single global result, which can significantly degrade performance for realms with many groups when the admin's visibility is granted at the all-groups level rather than via a role.

findings.title: Removed global-view short-circuit in getSubGroups causes a per-group authorization evaluation
findings.body: Similar to GroupsResource.getGroups, `getSubGroups` previously hoisted `canViewGlobal = auth.groups().canView()` out of the filter loop (`g -> canViewGlobal || auth.groups().canView(g)`), but now uses `.filter(auth.groups()::canView)` directly. Under FGAP V2, this forces a separate policy evaluation for every subgroup instead of computing the global permission once, which is a performance regression for groups with many subgroups when the caller only holds a blanket (all-groups) view permission rather than a role.

findings.title: No negative test verifying VIEW-only permission does not grant manage capability
findings.body: `testManageAllGroups()` only verifies that granting the MANAGE scope allows group creation/management; there is no test asserting that granting only the VIEW scope at the all-groups (or per-group) level does NOT allow create/update/delete operations. Such a test would have caught the bug in GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() where VIEW permission is mistakenly treated as sufficient for MANAGE-gated operations like creating top-level groups.

findings.title: Tests only exercise a single group, hiding getGroupIdsWithViewPermission correctness issues
findings.body: The membership-based tests (testCanViewUserByViewGroupMembers / testCanViewUserByManageGroupMembers) only create a single group with a single permission. Because `GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` incorrectly falls back to an 'all-groups' evaluation for every resource it iterates (see separate finding), a scenario with multiple groups - one with a scoped permission and one without - would be needed to detect that the method does not correctly restrict visibility to only the permitted group, and that the returned IDs are not valid group IDs usable by callers such as `getUsersCount`.
